statements.text: For hospitalisation reimbursement, you need to submit a duly completed claim form.
You must provide photo ID and age proof as part of the documents for hospitalisation reimbursement.

If hospitalisation occurred at a non-Network Provider, you must submit a copy of the hospital's registration certificate or registration number, or a certificate from hospital authorities stating the facilities available, including the number of beds.
A discharge card, day care summary, or transfer summary is required for hospitalisation reimbursement.
The final hospital bill, along with all original deposit and final payment receipts and refund receipts (if any advance was refunded), must be submitted.
For any implants used during surgery, you must submit the invoice, payment receipt, and implant stickers (e.g., lens sticker in cataract surgery, stent invoice and sticker in angioplasty surgery).
All previous consultation papers indicating the history and treatment details for the current illness, along with the advice for hospitalisation, must be submitted.
All diagnostic reports (including imaging and laboratory), along with the prescription by the medical practitioner and the invoice/bill with receipt from the diagnostic centre, are required.
All medicine or pharmacy bills, along with the prescription by the medical practitioner, must be submitted.
In accident cases, a copy of the MLC (Medical Legal Certificate) or FIR (First Information Report) is required.
In accident cases, a certification by the first treating doctor regarding history of alcohol consumption or any intoxication is required.
For death claims, a copy of the death summary and death certificate must be submitted.
Indoor case papers with nursing sheets detailing the medical history, treatment details, and patient’s progress must be submitted wherever required by the company.
An invoice for vaccination and the corresponding payment receipt must be submitted.
Original invoices for ambulance expenses, along with details of loss in the company’s prescribed format, must be submitted.
KYC documents of the policyholder as per AML guidelines are required for all claims above Rs 1 lakh.
A duly filled NEFT form with a cancelled blank cheque (with IFSC code, account number, and name mentioned) must be submitted.
A legal heir or succession certificate must be submitted wherever applicable.
Any other relevant document required by the company for claim assessment must be submitted.
The company only accepts bills, invoices, and medical treatment-related documents in the name of the insured person for whom the claim is submitted.
If original documents have been submitted to another insurer, the company will accept verified photocopies attested by that insurer, subject to the company’s satisfaction.

If requested by the company, the insured must undergo a medical examination by a doctor appointed by the company, at the company’s cost, and must allow inspection of medical and hospitalisation records.
The claim must be submitted within 30 days of the date of discharge from the hospital for hospitalisation reimbursement.
For post-hospitalisation expenses, the claim must be submitted within 15 days from the completion of post-hospitalisation treatment.
If original documents are submitted to the company and the insured requires them for claiming from another organization, the company will provide attested copies upon request.
If the required documents are not provided in full or are insufficient, the company may request additional information or documentation.

For pre- and post-hospitalisation or vaccination claims, a duly filled and signed claim form, photocopy of ID card or current year policy, original medicine bills with receipts and prescriptions, original investigation bills with receipts, prescriptions, and reports, original consultation documents and bills with receipts and prescriptions, and a copy of the discharge summary (except for outpatient dental claims) are required.

statements.text: You need a duly filled and signed Claim Form.

You need all previous consultation papers indicating the history and treatment details for the current illness and advice for hospitalization.
You need all diagnostic reports (including imaging and laboratory) along with the prescription by the medical practitioner and the invoice/bill with receipt from the diagnostic center.
You need the original discharge summary with the date of admission and discharge, clinical history, past history, procedure details, or day care summary from the hospital.
If the claim is for an accident, you need an MLC/FIR copy and a certificate from the first treating doctor regarding alcohol consumption or intoxication.
If the claim is above Rs 1 lakh, you need KYC documents as per AML guidelines.
If the claim is above Rs 1 lakh, you need a duly filled NEFT form with a cancelled blank cheque (with IFSC code, A/C number, and name mentioned on the cheque leaf).
If the claim is for death, you need the original death summary from the hospital and a copy of the death certificate from the treating doctor or hospital authority.
If the claim is for death and the claim is for the principal insured, you need a copy of the legal heir certificate.
You need the original invoice and payment receipt for ambulance expenses, if applicable, in the company's prescribed format.
You need the original invoice and payment receipt for vaccination, if applicable.

You need a copy of the hospital's registration certificate or registration number if hospitalization was at a non-network provider, or a certificate from hospital authorities providing facilities available, including the number of beds.
You need indoor case papers with a nursing sheet detailing the medical history, treatment details, and patient's progress, if required by the company.
